text.p: Salomon Brothers issued a buy recommendation for Israel's Teledata Communications, citing a promising outlook for the company's new products.
The company's products allow telecom operators to expand services in the access network by increasing the number of subscribers that may be served by new and existing infrastructure.
Teledata's order backlog has reached its highest level ever at over $32 million.

"Together with sales growth in the second quarter of 1996, gross margins are starting to recover to the levels that existed before the 1994-95 crisis, climbing above 47 percent versus 40 percent for the whole of 1995," analyst Victor Halpert said in a report.
"Although a higher proportion of lower margin sales is expected in the second half of 1996, overall gross profit margins should finish up at the 45 percent level."
Teledata's expected 1996 price/earnings ratio of 28.7 is trading at a discount to the market average of 36.4.

Halpert said the company enjoys promising growth opportunities in the fast expanding access-network segment of global telecommunications. It also has an impressive international presence with marketing channels in over 50 countries, he said.
The outlook for the company's new products is promising and the company is about to enter the world's largest telecommunications market, the United States, the report said.
